content.title: About
content.content: Welsh rarebit is a classic British dish consisting of toasted bread topped with a rich sauce made from melted cheese, mustard, beer and spices. It is usually served as a hot open‑face sandwich, sometimes garnished with herbs or tomato slices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “rarebit” is a humorous alteration of “rabbit”, although the dish contains no meat.
It originated in the 19th century and quickly became a staple in English pubs.
Traditional sauce uses cheddar cheese, but other cheeses such as gouda or Swiss can be used.
Worcestershire sauce and cayenne pepper are common additions for extra flavor.
Welsh rarebit is sometimes called “cheese on toast”, but the original sauce is thicker and more aromatic.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Cheese, the main ingredient, provides a high amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Cheese supplies complete protein that supports tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Cheese contains vitamin B12, which is important for nervous system function.

items.title: Benefits of mustard
items.content: Mustard adds selenium and antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: While cheese contains saturated fat, moderate portions can fit into a balanced diet.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy components may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Cheese and Worcestershire sauce can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins should avoid the dish.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is relatively high in calories due to cheese and butter, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Welsh rarebit hot, straight from the oven. Garnish with fresh herbs, tomato slices, or a sprinkle of paprika. It pairs well with a light salad or vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sauce can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Use fresh bread; if it has dried out, lightly toast it before adding the sauce.
